'''François Fages''' (August 23, 1959) is a French [[computer scientist]] known for contributions in the areas of [[Unification (computer science)|unification theory]], [[expert system|rule-based modelling]], [[logic programming]],<ref name="Codognet2001">{{cite book|author=Philippe Codognet|title=Logic Programming: 17th International Conference, ICLP 2001, Paphos, Cyprus, November 26 - December 1, 2001. Proceedings|url=https://archive.org/details/springer_10.1007-3-540-45635-X|date=14 November 2001|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-540-42935-7|pages=[https://archive.org/details/springer_10.1007-3-540-45635-X/page/n252 242]–}}</ref> [[concurrent constraint logic programming]],<ref name="BenhamouJussien2007">{{cite book|author1=Frédéric Benhamou|author2=Narendra Jussien|author3=Barry A. O'Sullivan|title=Trends in Constraint Programming|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0cwgAQAAIAAJ|date=25 May 2007|publisher=Wiley|isbn=978-1-905209-97-2}}</ref><ref name="MylopoulosReiter1991">{{cite book|author1=John Mylopoulos|author2=Ray Reiter|title=Advance Papers of the ... International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=w3xFAAAAYAAJ|year=1991|publisher=Morgan Kaufmann|isbn=978-1-55860-160-4|page=378}}</ref> [[computational biology]] and [[systems biology]].

==Early life and education==
Fages was born in Paris, France. He studied Mathematics and Physics at [[Université Paris-Sud]], Computer Science at the [[Université Pierre et Marie Curie]] and received his PhD from the [[Université Pierre et Marie Curie]] under the supervision of [[Gérard Huet]], in 1983 at age 23.

==Career==
Fages took a junior researcher position from [[CNRS]] at [[Ecole Normale Supérieure]], and became in addition, part-time teacher at [[Ecole Polytechnique]] from 1985 to 1998, and part-time consultant at Thomson-CSF (now [[Thales Group]]) research center from 1985 to 1996.
Since 1999, he is a senior researcher at the [[Institut national de recherche en informatique et en automatique]] (INRIA), the French national research institute on [[computer science]] and [[control theory|control]].<ref>[http://cordis.europa.eu/news/rcn/31957_en.html "EU project takes the pain out of packing"]. ''CORDIS''.</ref>

He is known in [[Unification (computer science)|unification theory]] for having shown the non-existence of minimal sets of unifiers in some equational theories (conjecture of Plotkin, 1972),<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Gordon|last1=Plotkin|title=Building-in equational theories|journal=Machine Intelligence|volume=7|pages=73–90|year=1972}}</ref>
and the decidability of associative-commutative unification<ref name="Jouannaud1985">{{cite book|author=Jean-Pierre Jouannaud|title=Rewriting Techniques and Applications: Dijon, France, May 20-22, 1985|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JH4yAAAAIAAJ|date=1 October 1985|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|isbn=978-3-540-15976-6}}</ref> in presence of several function symbols (conjecture of Stickel, 1981<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Mark|last1=Stickel|title=A Unification Algorithm for Associative-Commutative Functions|journal=Journal of the Association for Computing Machinery|volume=28|pages=423–434|year=1981|issue=3|doi=10.1145/322261.322262|s2cid=8163326 |doi-access=free}}</ref>).

In [[Production system (computer science)|rule-based modelling]], he is known for having created in 1988 a reactive rule-based language at Thomson-CSF (now Thalès group), which was later industrialized by [[ILOG]] (now IBM-Ilog) and became ILOG-Rules in 1996.

In [[logic programming]], Fages' theorem states that if a [[logic programming|normal logic program]] is positive-order-consistent—that is, there is no infinite sequence of ground atoms a<sub>0</sub>, a<sub>1</sub>, a<sub>2</sub>, ... related by positive dependencies from a<sub>i+1</sub> to a<sub>i</sub> in the atom dependency graph—then the [[stable model semantics|stable models]] of the program coincide with the two-valued Herbrand models of its [[Negation as failure|Clark's completion]].
<ref>Fages, François (1994). "Consistency of Clark's Completion and the Existence of Stable Models". ''Journal of Methods of Logic in Computer Science'', 1(1), 51–60.</ref>
This result has shown useful for implementing [[stable model semantics]] with classical [[propositional satisfiability]] solvers.<ref>Erdem, Esra; Lifschitz, Vladimir; (2001) "Fages' Theorem for Programs with Nested Expressions". ''Proc. ICLP 2001'':242-254, MIT Press.</ref>
This theorem has also been generalized to [[logic programming|disjunctive logic programs]].
<ref>Lee, Joohyung, and Vladimir Lifschitz. "Loop formulas for disjunctive logic programs." In Logic Programming: 19th International Conference, ICLP 2003, Mumbai, India, December 9-13, 2003. Proceedings 19, pp. 451-465. Springer Berlin Heidelberg, 2003.</ref>

In [[concurrent constraint logic programming]], he has established with Paul Ruet and Sylvain Soliman the logical semantics of concurrent constraint programs in [[Jean-Yves Girard]]'s [[linear logic]].
This result has been generalized to [[Constraint handling rules]]<ref>Betz, Hariolf; Frühwirth, Thom (2005). "A Linear-Logic Semantics for Constraint Handling Rules". ''Proc. Principles and Practice of Constraint Programming - CP 2005'':137-151, Springer-Verlag.</ref> and to the asynchronous [[Pi-calculus]].<ref>Palamidessi, Catuscia; Saraswat, Vijay; Valencia, Franck (2006). "On the Expressiveness of Linearity vs Persistence in the Asychronous Pi-Calculus". ''Proc. Logic in Computer Science - LICS 2006'':59-68.</ref>

In 2010 Fages co-ordinated a project to use mathematics to improve the packing of light bulbs and other oddly shaped products.<ref>[http://cacm.acm.org/news/79704-softwares-take-on-the-light-bulb-joke/fulltext "Mixing Math and Expertise"]. ''Communications of the ACM'', March 12, 2010</ref>

In 2014 Fages works in [[computational biology|computational]] [[systems biology]],
coordinates the development of the Biochemical Abstract Machine (BIOCHAM) rule-based modeling and logical analysis software and studies biochemical processes in the [[cell cycle]] and in [[cell signaling]].

In 2014, he received the [[:fr:Prix Monpetit|Monpetit Prize]] from the [[French Academy of Sciences]].<ref>[http://www.sciencesmaths-paris.fr/fr/chercheurs-primes-59.htm "Chercheurs primés"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150922110324/http://www.sciencesmaths-paris.fr/fr/chercheurs-primes-59.htm |date=2015-09-22 }}. ''Foundation Sciences'', 2015.</ref>
